title: Relay Loss in Mesh Topology
description: This scenario explores relay loss dynamics within a mesh communication topology. The disturbance creates coordination challenges that test the agents' ability to adapt, communicate effectively, and maintain freight flow under adverse conditions.
edge_cases_to_watch: Partial Information Asymmetry: Agents b, c, and d know agent a is silent, but agents assigned to work with a may assume physical failure vs comms failure.
Information Cascades: A failure to pass status updates from agent a via mesh neighbors leads to outdated routing decisions for the remaining active agents.
Ghost Reservations: Agent a may have reserved route capacity before silence; remaining agents must decide whether to wait for a-to-clear or assume capacity is permanently blocked.
Redundant Path Utilization: Testing if agents switch to longer physical routes to compensate for the loss of 'a' as a coordination hub.
coordination_challenges: Distributed Consensus: Reaching agreement on the state of the network without input from agent 'a'.
Dynamic Re-routing: Recalculating freight paths when the primary coordinator/relay is no longer broadcasting intent.
Deadlock Avoidance: Preventing two agents from entering a low-capacity route (e.g., east-north) due to lack of coordination messages from the muted agent.
suggested_agent_strategies: Gossip Protocol: Agents should broadcast status updates to all neighbors to ensure information spreads despite node loss.
Proactive Buffer Management: Agents should reserve slightly more capacity than needed when a primary peer is silent to account for uncertainty.
Fallback to Local Autonomy: If communication timeouts occur, agents should transition from 'collaborative optimization' to 'local greedy optimization' to maintain throughput.
Heartbeat Verification: Implementation of rapid periodic pings to minimize the 'detection_turns' impact.

coordination_challenges: Mesh connectivity preservation despite single-node silence
Information decay management during the timeout period

success_criteria: Agents adapt communication to topology constraints
Recovery from disruption within expected turns
Minimal capacity wastage due to 'ghost' reservations
